transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Alex Rivera (Crestline), Priya Nair (Crestline SRE), Liam O'Sullivan (CTO), Samira Khan (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift, adding EU and APAC regions, and contract extension terms. Customer is evaluating mix of Dedicated vs Hosted and an on-prem/private pilot for sensitive workloads. Discussed latency targets, audit logs/KMS, and provisional pricing with burst capacity.

Topics covered:
- Renewal cadence and desired term length
- Capacity forecast (Q2-Q4) and burst needs
- Regional onboarding: EU then APAC, edge locations
- Private deployment pilot for PII workloads, encryption/KMS & SOC2 details
- Next steps: quote revision, runbook, pilot benchmark window

Action items noted (informal): Jordan to revise quote; Maya to share runbook; Crestline to send traffic numbers; Diego to coordinate pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we scheduled 45 minutes to walk through the renewal and the regional acceleration plan. quick round-robin?
[00:12] Alex: Hi all hi Jordan Alex here from Platform, I'll be focusing on capacity and ops constraints.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, SRE, hi.
[00:20] Liam: Liam, CTO, short on time, listening for major blockers.
[00:24] Samira: Samira procurement, also on call for contract questions.
[00:28] Maya: Maya from Redwood SE, I'll go through technical pieces later.
[00:31] Diego: Diego CSM, I'll follow up on pilot scheduling.
[00:36] Jordan: Awesome. quick context — Crestline's current contract ends in late March, you flagged wanting to expand EU first and then APAC and also test private for a subset of workloads, is that right?
[00:48] Alex: Yep that's correct. EU is highest priority for our customers in fintech verticals. APAC is next, but we need assurance on latency and on data residency.
[00:58] Priya: Also, for certain flows we need HSM-backed keys and audit log retention longer than one year, that came up in the security review.
[01:06] Jordan: Noted. on the contract side we can propose a 12 or 24 month extension with committed Dedicated capacity and optional burst pool. we did a quick cost delta that we'll formalize, but we wanted to check the traffic shape first.
[01:19] Alex: Traffic is spiky — weekends low, weekdays peak midday and again at 19:00 UTC. Burst is important for campaigns.
[01:27] Maya: For latency targets, are you aiming sub-250ms p50 for user-facing completions, or is 300-400ms acceptable?
[01:36] Alex: Ideally <250ms p50.  p95 we can tolerate up to 600ms for complex requests. but the p50 is more customer-facing.
[01:44] Maya: Okay, that helps kernel selection and routing policy, we can recommend model variants that fit those SLOs.
[01:50] [00:60] Liam: Quick question on private pilot — will that be fully on-prem or VPC-hosted with private control plane? We have compliance teams leaning to VPC but some PII flows may need on-prem.
[02:01] Maya: We can do either. typical flow we see: start with VPC private deployment for isolation then run a small on-prem POC for the truly air-gapped workloads. the runtime is the same but provisioning differs; there are a few network prerequisites.
[02:14] Priya: For KMS, can you integrate with our HSM (AWS CloudHSM) and rotate keys via our KMS policy?
[02:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, and we can map key rotation policies. we'll add the KMS integration notes in the runbook.
[02:27] Jordan: On pricing — we have three levers: committed dedicated capacity, burst pool, and hosted pay-as-you-go. We suggested a tiered burst discount if you commit more baseline throughput.
[02:37] Samira: We need clear numbers. procurement will want committed units, uplift rates, and termination terms. also what's the SLA for region activation?
[02:45] Diego: Typically region activation for EU is 4-6 weeks after contract finalization if we have predictable capacity and infra approvals; APAC 6-9 weeks depending on edge footprint.
[02:57] Alex: 4–6 weeks is tight, but okay if we start paperwork now. do you require infra IP allowlists or peering?
[03:05] Maya: For Private we need VPC peering and some routes; for Dedicated in our hosted offering we can do overlay peering and less customer infra changes. we'll include a checklist.
[03:14] [03:14] (audio glitch)
[03:18] Alex: sorry I missed that last bit, can you repeat?
[03:21] Jordan: yes — for Dedicated hosted regions we handle most infra, Private requires peering and route setup.
[03:28] Priya: For audit logs and retention, is there an option to export to our SIEM? Splunk right now?
[03:34] Maya: Yes we can forward audit logs to Splunk or S3 with encryption, retention policies can be configured, and we support FIPS endpoints for log push.
[03:42] Liam: On reliability, what happens if a region suffers capacity constraints? Do you have automatic fallback to another region or model variant?
[03:50] Maya: We support smart routing and fallback policies — you can define priority: EU primary then fallback to hosted in US with reduced throughput, or fallback to a smaller quantized model. It's configurable per route.
[03:59] Alex: Okay good. we worry about data crossing borders though — fallbacks can't send PII to another region.
[04:06] Jordan: right, for PII we'd tie routes to no-cross-region policies and the fallback could be local smaller instance or delay until capacity restored.
[04:14] Samira: Contract question — can we add a clause for region activation SLAs and credits if activation slips beyond X weeks?
[04:20] Jordan: We can include activation SLAs; credits for missed activation are possible but limited. I'll have legal draft language.
[04:27] Priya: Also need SOC2 + ISO docs and recent pen-test report.
[04:31] Maya: we'll share our security pack and the latest SOC2 report, plus the pen test summary.
[04:36] Diego: I'll attach the security doc link in the follow-up email and Jordan will attach the revised quote.
[04:41] [05:00] (background)
[04:45] Alex: about pilot benchmark — can you run a 24-hour synthetic workload mimicking our peak, and show latency/cost profiles?
[04:52] Maya: Yes, we can run an ingress benchmark. for private on-prem pilot we'll need a test image and some sample traffic; for dedicated hosted we'll spin up a burst pool and run the same workload.
[05:02] Alex: Great. also, for the burst pricing, can you show committed vs no-commit scenario side-by-side?
[05:08] Jordan: we'll include a spreadsheet that shows committed baseline, cost per token, and burst unit price, plus an example monthly bill for your forecast.
[05:15] Priya: For APAC activation, any special hardware constraints? We use T4/RTX families on prem, but in APAC we prefer lower-latency GCUs.
[05:24] Maya: We'll propose model/instance families per region; APAC footprints sometimes use different GPU mix but we can recommend quantized variants if cost sensitivity exists.
[05:33] Liam: One more thing — SSO/SAML and RBAC. We need admin separation between infra ops and product teams.
[05:40] Maya: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and role-based policies. we can demo the RBAC mapping in the console if helpful.
[05:48] Samira: On termination clauses — if we do 24 months we need a flexible exit for a major regulatory change.
[05:53] Jordan: acceptable, we'll put a regulatory-change carveout into the term sheet for legal review.
[05:59] [06:00] Diego: quick recap then next steps: Jordan to send quote, Maya runbook + benchmark plan, Crestline to share traffic and decision timeline.
[06:10] Alex: decision timeline — we want the procurement review by 2027-02-18 and finalize by end of Feb if numbers look reasonable.
[06:18] Jordan: great. we'll aim to deliver the materials by 2/7 to give you time.
[06:24] Priya: can we also get a list of model variants you recommend for 250ms p50?
[06:29] Maya: yes I'll include recommended model profiles and expected p50/p95 under your workload in the benchmark doc.
[06:36] Liam: ok thanks everyone.
[06:38] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the quote. Diego will pick a pilot date. End meeting.

References & shared links (mentioned during call):
- Pricing spreadsheet (to be attached): https://redwood.example/decks/crestline-pricing-v2.xlsx
- EU/APAC runbook draft (will share): https://redwood.example/runbooks/eu-apac-onboard-v1.pdf
- Security pack (SOC2 + pen test summary): https://redwood.example/security/crestline-pack

Questions raised:
- Can fallbacks be restricted to region-local resources for PII flows? (answered: yes, via route policy)
- What is exact activation SLA for regions? (Jordan: propose inclusion; will get legal language)
- Can audit logs be pushed to Splunk and retained >1yr? (answered: yes)

End of transcript.
